system_description.narrative_title: U.S. securing control and investment in Venezuela's oil reserves
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is that the U.S. is negotiating to secure long-term access, control and investment positions in Venezuela's vast oil reserves—including reported Pentagon stakes and deals with U.S. firms—to refill U.S. strategic stockpiles and reshape supply. As an open system this involves cross-border flows of oil, capital, legal authority, and political legitimacy, producing market, diplomatic and domestic feedbacks that propagate through prices, alliances, and sanction regimes. The proposed multi-decade arrangements and reported 65 billion-barrel figure are generating controversy inside Venezuela and internationally, tying energy security directly to geopolitical and electoral dynamics.
system_description.scope: Inside the system boundary: concrete actors (U.S. executive branch/Trump administration, Pentagon, Chevron and other oil firms, Venezuelan interim government and local investors such as Betancourt, Energean/BP asset talks), assets and events (Venezuela's proven reserves ~65bn barrels, proposed 25-year deals, SPR refilling), processes and systemic variables (long-term access agreements, equity stakes, capital flows, oil export volumes, market price signals, legal/sovereignty disputes, political legitimacy and domestic backlash).
system_description.super_system: Global energy markets and international geopolitical order
adjacent_subsystems: U.S. domestic politics and electoral signaling
Latin American regional sovereignty and diplomatic relations
Global oil market dynamics and OPEC+ supply politics
International law, sanctions regime and foreign investment security

variables.name: Proven oil reserves
variables.description: The estimated quantity of commercially recoverable crude oil in the affected hydrocarbon basins measured in barrels.

variables.name: Extent of long‑term access agreements
variables.description: The aggregate scope and coverage of multi‑year contracts and legal arrangements granting external parties access to reservoir production and infrastructure.

variables.name: Equity stake share
variables.description: The proportion of ownership interests held by non‑domestic investors across upstream oil assets expressed as a percentage of total equity.

variables.name: Capital inflows to oil sector
variables.description: The rate and magnitude of financial investment (debt and equity) entering upstream and midstream hydrocarbon projects over time.

variables.name: Oil export volume
variables.description: The volumetric flow of crude oil and condensates leaving the domestic production system for external markets per unit time.

variables.name: Strategic stockpile level
variables.description: The quantity of crude and refined petroleum held in official strategic reserves available for national emergency or market intervention.

variables.name: Global oil price
variables.description: The market price signal for crude oil that reflects global supply‑demand balances and guides investment and production decisions.

variables.name: Sanction enforcement level
variables.description: The intensity and strictness with which trade, financial and asset restrictions are implemented against relevant economic actors.

variables.name: Legal control authority
variables.description: The de facto degree of recognized legal or administrative control over hydrocarbon assets and revenue streams within the jurisdiction.

variables.name: Domestic political legitimacy
variables.description: The perceived legitimacy of governing arrangements among the domestic population and key domestic constituencies.

variables.name: Domestic backlash intensity
variables.description: The magnitude and frequency of public protests, political opposition actions, and societal resistance against energy sector decisions.

variables.name: International diplomatic alignment
variables.description: The degree of support or opposition among external states and international actors toward the access and investment arrangements.

variables.name: Military involvement level
variables.description: The extent to which armed forces or defense institutions are engaged in securing, administering, or protecting hydrocarbon assets and flows.

variables.name: Contract duration commitment
variables.description: The average remaining length of time (in years) that binding access or investment contracts commit parties to specified terms.

variables.name: Production capacity utilization
variables.description: The percent of installed upstream production and midstream processing capacity that is being actively used at a given time.

variables.name: Oil supply security risk perception
variables.description: The perceived probability and expected impact of disruptions to oil supply chains affecting market participants and planners.

catalysts.title: Signing of US–Venezuela long‑term oil access agreement
catalysts.description: Formal signing and legal ratification of the announced long‑term access/investment deal between US entities and Venezuela's oil sector.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple reports say US nears deal and will take control / invest (Aug 28-29 headlines).

catalysts.title: Formal approval of Pentagon's 35% stake
catalysts.description: DoD/administration formalizes the reported 35% Pentagon equity stake in the Venezuelan oil venture.
catalysts.rationale: WSJ and other reports: Pentagon to take 35% stake; headlines describe plan and criticism (Aug 30).

catalysts.title: Chevron deal closing and project expansion
catalysts.description: Chevron finalizes migration of projects and commits to expansion investments in Venezuelan oil fields.
catalysts.rationale: Reports say Chevron to complete deal, migrate and expand projects; other US firms near investments (Aug 29 headlines).

catalysts.title: Start of SPR refill using Venezuelan oil
catalysts.description: Physical shipments and receipt of Venezuelan crude into the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve begin.
catalysts.rationale: Trump stated US will refill the SPR using Venezuelan oil (Aug 30 headlines).

catalysts.title: Ratification of 25‑year access contract
catalysts.description: Formal ratification and implementation of the reported 25‑year access and investment commitment by Venezuelan authorities.
catalysts.rationale: Venezuelan interim president said the US energy deal will last 25 years (Reuters, Aug 30).

catalysts.title: Escalation of domestic political backlash
catalysts.description: Increased protests, denunciations and political mobilization in Venezuela opposing the US oil deal, generating legal and operational friction.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines say the oil deal is denounced by both sides and draws criticism (Aug 30).

catalysts.title: US congressional or legal challenge to the deal
catalysts.description: Congressional hearings, legislation or lawsuits in the US aimed at blocking or constraining the Venezuela oil deal or Pentagon stake.
catalysts.rationale: Deal provokes criticism and is politically controversial in US; legal/legislative challenges likely (multiple headlines).

catalysts.title: Commencement of Venezuelan oil shipments to US
catalysts.description: First commercial shipments of Venezuelan crude destined for US buyers or SPR delivery depart Venezuelan ports.
catalysts.rationale: Statements about using Venezuelan oil to refill US reserves and US taking control imply imminent shipments (Aug 28-30 headlines).
